Fireside chat used to reframe the narrative after a sharp post-Q3 stock decline; no headline period results.

Q3 2025 called a phenomenal quarter on top line, gross margin and EBITDA margin; the net-sales 'disconnect' (vs buy-side) driven primarily by promotional activity bringing Celsius cases back at a lower net sales per case, plus Amazon Prime load-in timing.
Q3 2024 included inventory optimization - Q3 2023 to Q3 2025 volume up ~10-11%, so straight YoY reads are distorted.
Brand Celsius turnaround: from negative low-single-digit scanner growth early 2025 to double digits and category-exceeding performance, ~20% in convenience - credited to the Live Fit Go campaign.
'High 80s' percent of the Alani US DSD system migrated into Pepsi as of December 1; methodical step-by-step integration (Tier 3/4 in Q1, Tier 1/2 across Q1-Q2).
Q4 2025 will see the most gross-margin pressure - integration one-time charges, Pepsi-transition returns/scrap, tariffs, lower-margin Rockstar mix, rising aluminum/Midwest premium.
Sequential margin recovery path: Q4 pressured, each step Q4-Q1-Q2 improving, back to low 50s by back half 2026, expanding into Q4 2026 and 2027.
Potential Pepsi year-end inventory drawdown framed as immaterial timing (~$5M/day); on a $2B+ business a couple days either way doesn't warrant a line in the sand.
Rockstar revenue partly recognized as finished-goods top line, partly as a brand-transition service in other income - a presentation nuance during integration.
RGM (revenue growth management) a big focus for 2026+; pricing seen as an opportunity but nothing specific to call out; RGM team built out (Eric brought on March 2025).
Captaincy lets the company control PepsiCo planogram space - 'put the fast cars on the track', often more Celsius on shelf.

Alani LTO model addresses the 'treadmill' concern - LTOs drive trial and frequency, the whole brand is lifted with a net gain after each LTO, and strong non-seasonal LTOs can become permanent power SKUs.
First Celsius LTO (Spritz Vibe) was the top velocity item and provided key learnings ahead of running LTOs with Alani inside the Pepsi system.
Rockstar adds a sugar-segment play (just under 50% of the category) where only two primary players exist; intentional SKU rationalization toward ~$250M; bullish but not overnight.
Capital allocation: number one priority is investing behind the business; opportunistic buyback when a value gap exists (has been in the market); debt paydown.
Senior hires (Eric Hanson President/COO, Rishi CMO ex-16-yr Pepsi, Garrett international) viewed as positive for the Pepsi relationship and the three-brand portfolio.
Long-term: a marathon not a sprint - does not expect to catch Red Bull/Monster in 2026 but aims to keep climbing share, over-indexing with sugar-free, female and Gen Z consumers.
Fireside-chat format - no formal management prepared remarks; all substantive content is Q&A.
What happened in Q3 2025 on Celsius shipments vs cycling last year's inventory reductions, and what did the market misunderstand?

Q3 a phenomenal quarter; a disconnect in brand Celsius net sales - in line with sell-side but below buy-side; Q3 2024 included optimization, Q3 2023 to Q3 2025 volume up ~10-11%; the real disconnect was promotional activity bringing cases back at a lower net sales per case, plus Amazon Prime load-in timing.
Three days into the Alani-into-Pepsi move plus Rockstar integration, is there better visibility on Q4 top line and margin?

~80% (actually high 80s) of the Alani US DSD system into Pepsi as of 12/1, on plan; Q4 carries timing/sequencing of the Rockstar integration (finished goods to top line, brand-transition service to other income) and methodical step-by-step Alani integration (Tier 3/4 in Q1, Tier 1/2 across Q1-Q2); typical year-end cash management, nothing material.
Given the $100M+ Q3 2024 history and ~$5M per day, how to frame potential year-end inventory management?
If Pepsi shut down for a week there could be an impact of that magnitude, but it is immaterial timing rather than a new program.
Does management have communication/visibility that a year-end drawdown is happening, or is it just leaving cushion?

On a $2B+ business a couple of days either way doesn't warrant a line in the sand; integrations going well - Alani completes by Q1, Rockstar in H1 2026; typical CPG year-end cash management, nothing material; set up for a fantastic 2026.
Why has energy been more resilient than broader CPG, and how to maintain Celsius/Alani momentum if the consumer weakens?

Even when energy was flat last year it outperformed CPG peers; 2025 a substantial bounce back driven by Alani, a strong Monster year, solid Red Bull year and the Celsius turnaround; consumers want better-for-you, healthier, sugar-free products and females are entering the category - a sweet spot for Celsius/Alani.
How is Celsius thinking about taking pricing - lift, promo optimization, or RGM?

Agrees there is price elasticity and opportunity; focus on price-pack and promotional activity across the three-brand portfolio and building a revenue growth management team (Eric brought on March 2025); pricing a tool in the belt, RGM a big focus for 2026 and beyond.
Puts and takes on gross margin and OpEx for 2026, and confidence in getting back to low 50s then mid-50s gross margin.

Q4 2025 the most pressure (integration one-time charges, Pepsi-transition returns/scrap, tariffs, lower-margin Rockstar); Alani fully into the orbit structure by Q1, synergies fully baked from April; Rockstar mostly done by Q1; back half 2026 margins return to low 50s; big beverage second line online Q3, fully baked Q4, enabling continued expansion into 2027.
How does Celsius keep brand-Celsius momentum going in 2026 and longer term?

Live Fit Go campaign broadened the message and captured new consumers; will continue to invest with more efficiency; the captaincy program is a key opportunity, with Celsius likely getting more shelf space as the fast cars on the track.
Where do brand Celsius market shares stand in developed markets, and how does growth in mature vs less-mature markets look?

South Florida low-20s to mid-20s, NYC high teens/~20, other major markets 15-20%, under-indexed markets upper single digits; #2 energy brand on Amazon; blue-sky markets can still reach mid-to-upper teens, just taking a bit longer than anticipated 1.5 years ago.
Learnings from the first brand-Celsius LTO (Spritz Vibe) and plans for Celsius LTOs in 2026 and broader innovation for 2027.

Spritz Vibe was the top velocity item and provided key learnings ahead of running LTOs with Alani inside the Pepsi system - goal is flawless execution; a new Pepsi-affiliated Board member helps cut through Pepsi-system dynamics; feels good about 2026 LTO strategy.
What is the ultimate distribution potential for Alani relative to fully-distributed Celsius, and what gap should exist?

Alani on a path to a similar ACV to Celsius, achieved methodically; somewhat farther along than Celsius was at its Pepsi entry; independent convenience should drive Alani ACV to a mid-90 level; full visibility into the business by end of Q2 2026 once resets complete.
Alani long-term growth & LTO treadmill risk
Long-term growth for Alani given LTOs are so central, and the concern about the treadmill of cycling prior-year LTOs.

LTOs drive both trial (new consumers) and frequency; data shows the entire brand is lifted with a net gain after an LTO concludes, core SKUs continue to perform; Alani carries fewer SKUs than Celsius; well-performing non-seasonal LTOs can be brought into permanent rotation as power SKUs.
How does Rockstar fit into the portfolio, and the plans to stabilize and grow it vs willingness to cannibalize space?

The August transactions were about owning the Pepsi-system energy portfolio (the captaincy); Rockstar adds an energy-focused asset with internal expertise; intentional SKU rationalization toward a ~$250M FY2026 run rate frees space for faster SKUs; Rockstar plays in the sugar segment (just under 50% of category); bullish but not overnight.
What is Celsius doing to protect its positioning and moat in sugar-free active-lifestyle energy, and what differentiates the brand?

Sugar-free is what drives the category (health and wellness, functional fitness, lifestyle); the category has always been competitive; Celsius and Alani well positioned with authentic fitness/gym roots (Alani founded in GNC, Celsius born in the gyms); authenticity and trend alignment are differentiators.
Has the company been in the market on the $300M repurchase authorization, and what are the broader capital allocation priorities?

Strong cash generation; ~$200M used to pay down debt; number one priority is investing behind the business and portfolio growth; with a strong balance sheet the company went into the market to repurchase stock when it saw a value gap - confirmed it has been buying shares.
What do the recent senior hires bring, and any impact on the Pepsi relationship?

Positive impact on the Pepsi relationship; Eric Hanson brings commercialization, portfolio and RGM experience for the three-brand portfolio and DSD work; Rishi (16 years at Pepsi) brings multi-brand management as a 'conductor'; Garrett brings international relationships across Europe and Asia.
Live Fit Go investment & multi-brand marketing
Investment plans for Live Fit Go and how to balance investments across the brands.

Live Fit Go is Celsius-specific, will continue to be invested in during 2026 with greater efficiency, one of several key media programs; marketing restructured with dedicated brand teams over Celsius, Alani and Rockstar; Rishi the conductor; the Alani marketing team retained and cofounders Max and Trey remain involved to preserve Alani's voice.
How does the category structure develop as Celsius gains share, given Monster and Red Bull hold ~70% combined, and what differentiates Celsius from prior challengers?

Praised Red Bull and Monster's track record; feels good at close to 20% portfolio share; the key is capitalizing on trends - sugar-free, females, Gen Z, where Celsius and Alani over-index; a marathon not a sprint - does not expect to catch anyone in 2026 but aims to keep climbing share and expects to be among the biggest beneficiaries of category growth.
